gaps.sentence: The audience found the lecture extremely ___ (BORE).
gaps.explanation: The lecture causes boredom, so it is boring; the audience would be bored.

gaps.sentence: His ___ (DETERMINE) to become a doctor never wavered.
gaps.explanation: A noun is needed after 'His': determination (-ation noun); 'determined' is the adjective.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ to accept the conditions at first (WILLING).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: she did not want to
gaps.explanation: 'At first' suggests reluctance, so the negative adjective 'unwilling' (un- + willing) is needed.

gaps.sentence: She was fired for ___ behaviour at work (PROFESSIONAL).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed before the noun 'behaviour'
gaps.explanation: The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unprofessional behaviour is behaviour below professional standards.

gaps.sentence: There was a lot of ___ (OPPOSE) to the new road.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of' needs a noun: opposition (-tion noun); 'opposite' is an adjective or noun meaning the contrary.

gaps.sentence: When the costs rose, we had to ___ our plans (CONSIDER).
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again: reconsider means to think about something again. A base verb follows 'had to'.

gaps.sentence: We had no ___ (CHOOSE) but to cancel the trip.
gaps.explanation: 'Have no choice but to do something' is the fixed phrase; the noun of 'choose' is an irregular 'choice'.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (INTERVIEW) asked her some difficult questions.
gaps.hint: the person who asks the questions (-er = doer)
gaps.explanation: The interviewer asks; the interviewee answers. The suffix -er marks the doer.
